If he comes in alone, he shall go out alone; but if a wife comes in with him, his wife shall also go out with him.
But if his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and the children shall be his master’s, and he shall go out alone.
But if the slave answers and says, ‘I love my master, and my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,’
his master shall bring him before God’s tribunal, and then bring him to the door, to the doorpost. His master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him for ever.
And if a man sells his own daughter as a household slave, she shall not go out as the female slaves go out.
If she does not please her master, who pledged her to himself, he shall redeem her; he has no right to sell her to a foreign nation, because he has broken faith with her.
But if he pledges her to his son, he shall deal with her according to the ordinance for daughters.
And if he takes another wife to himself, he shall not deprive her of her necessities, her clothing, or her conjugal companionship.
But if he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out freely, without silver.
And if a man strikes another, and he dies, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death.
But if he did not act willingly, and God delivered him into his hands, I will give you a place where the slayer shall flee.
But if a man attacks his neighbour to kill him by deceit, and flees for refuge, you shall take him from My altar to put him to death.
He who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
He who reviles his father or his mother shall surely die.
And if a man steals one of the sons of Israel, and overpowers him and sells him, and he is found with him, he shall surely die.
And if two men quarrel, and one strikes his neighbour with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die, but lies on his bed,
if the man rises and walks outside with a staff, the one who struck him shall be guiltless; only he shall pay for his lost labour and his healing.
And if a man strikes his male slave or his female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his hands, he shall surely be avenged by judgment.
But if the slave survives a day or two, he shall not be avenged; for he is his silver.

And if two men fight and strike a woman with child, and her child comes out not fully formed, he shall surely be fined; as the woman’s husband shall impose on him, he shall pay according to an assessment.
But if it was fully formed, he shall give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
And if a man strikes the eye of his household slave or of his female slave, and blinds it, he shall set them free for their eye.
And if he knocks out the tooth of his household slave or of his female slave, he shall set them free for their tooth.
And if a bull gores a man or a woman, and the person dies, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall be guiltless.
But if the bull was in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, and it kills a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner also shall die.
But if a ransom is imposed on him, he shall give for the ransom of his life all that they impose on him.
Whether it gores a son or a daughter, they shall deal with him according to this ordinance.
And if the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.
And if a man opens a pit, or hews out a pit, and does not cover it, and a calf or donkey falls in it,
the owner of the pit shall make restitution. He shall give silver to the animal’s owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
And if a man’s bull gores his neighbour’s bull, and it dies, they shall sell the living bull and divide its silver; and they shall also divide the dead bull.
But if the bull is known to have been in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, he shall repay bull for bull; and the dead bull shall be his.
And if a man steals a calf or a sheep, and slaughters it or sells it, he shall repay five calves for the calf, and four sheep for the sheep.”
“And if the thief is found breaking in, and is struck and dies, there is no murder in his case.
But if the sun has risen upon him, he is guilty; he shall die in return. And if he has nothing, let him be sold for the theft.
But if he is caught, and the stolen thing is found alive in his hand, from donkey to sheep, he shall repay them double.

And if a man grazes a field or a vineyard, and lets his beast graze another field, he shall repay from his own field according to its yield; but if it grazes the whole field, he shall repay the best of his field and the best of his vineyard.
And if fire breaks out and catches thorns, and burns a threshing floor, or standing grain, or a plain, he who kindled the fire shall make restitution.
And if a man gives his neighbour silver or goods to keep, and they are stolen from the man’s house, if the thief is found, he shall repay double.
But if the thief is not found, the master of the house shall come before God and swear that he has not dealt wickedly with any of his neighbour’s deposit.

In every alleged wrong concerning a calf, beast of burden, sheep, garment, or any disputed loss, whatever it may be, the case of both parties shall come before God. Whoever is convicted through God shall repay his neighbour double.
And if a man gives his neighbour a beast of burden, or a calf, or a sheep, or any beast to keep, and it is injured, or dies, or is taken captive, and no one knows,
an oath by God shall be between them that he has not acted dishonestly concerning any of his neighbour’s deposit. The owner shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.
But if it was stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
If it was taken by a wild animal, he shall bring the owner to the prey, and he shall not make restitution.
And if a man borrows from his neighbour, and it is injured, or dies, or is taken captive, and its owner is not with it, he shall make restitution.
But if its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution; and if it is hired, it shall be reckoned against its hire.
And if a man deceives a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he shall surely give the marriage payment for her to be his wife.
But if her father firmly refuses, and is unwilling to give her to him as a wife, he shall pay silver to the father according to the marriage payment for virgins.
You shall not preserve sorcerers alive.
Everyone who lies with a beast, you shall surely put to death.
He who sacrifices to gods, except to the Lord alone, shall surely be destroyed.
And you shall not ill-treat a resident foreigner, neither shall you afflict him; for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you afflict them, and they cry aloud to Me, I will surely listen to their voice,
I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
And if you lend silver to your poor brother beside you, you shall not press him hard, neither shall you lay interest upon him.
And if you take your neighbour’s garment in pledge, you shall restore it to him before the setting of the sun;
for this is his covering, his only garment for his nakedness; What shall he sleep in? If therefore he cries to Me, I will listen to him; for I am merciful.
You shall not revile gods, neither shall you speak evil of the rulers of your people.
You shall not delay the firstfruits of your threshing floor and your winepress; you shall give Me the firstborn of your sons.
You shall do the same with your calf, and your sheep, and your beast of burden; it shall be under its mother for seven days, and on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
You shall be holy people to Me. You shall not eat flesh taken by wild animals; throw it to the dog.”
“You shall not receive an empty report. You shall not agree with the unrighteous to become an unrighteous witness.
You shall not join the many in evil; neither shall you join a multitude in turning aside with the many, to turn aside judgment.
Neither shall you favour a poor man in judgment.
And if you meet your enemy’s ox or his beast of burden wandering, you shall surely turn it back and restore it to him.
And if you see your enemy’s beast of burden fallen beneath its load, you shall not pass it by; but you shall raise it up together with him.
You shall not pervert the judgment of a poor man in his cause.
You shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, neither shall you justify the ungodly for gifts.
And you shall receive no gifts; for gifts blind the eyes of those who see, and corrupt righteous words.
And you shall not afflict a resident foreigner; for you know the soul of the resident foreigner, since you yourselves were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
For six years you shall sow your land, and gather its produce;

but in the seventh you shall grant it release, and leave it; and the poor of your nation shall eat, and what they leave the wild beasts shall eat. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.

For six days you shall do your works, but on the seventh day there shall be rest, that your ox and your beast of burden may rest, and that the son of your female slave and the resident foreigner may be refreshed.
Keep everything I have said to you. Do not call to mind the name of other gods or let it be heard from your mouth.
Three times a year you shall keep a feast to Me.

Keep the feast of unleavened bread; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of new grain; for in it you came out of Egypt. You shall not appear before Me empty-handed.

And you shall keep the feast of harvest, of the firstfruits of your labours which you sow in your field; and the feast of completion as the year goes out, when you gather your labours out of your field.
Every male of yours shall appear three times in the year before the Lord your God.
For when I cast out nations before you, and enlarge your borders, you shall not sacrifice the blood of My offering with leaven, neither shall the fat of My feast remain until morning.
You shall bring the firstfruits of the first produce of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.
And behold, I send My angel before your face, to keep you in the way, that he may bring you into the land which I have prepared for you.
Take care, and listen to him, and do not disobey him; for he shall not yield before you, for My name is upon him.

If you diligently listen to My voice, and you do all that I command you, and you keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine, and you shall be to Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation. You shall say these words to the sons of Israel: ‘If you diligently listen to My voice, and you do all that I say to you, I will be an enemy to your enemies, and oppose those who oppose you.’
For My angel shall go before you, and bring you to the Amorite, and Hittite, and Perizzite, and Canaanite, and Girgashite, and Hivite, and Jebusite; and I will destroy them.
You shall not bow down to their gods, neither shall you serve them, nor do according to their works; but you shall utterly overthrow them, and utterly shatter their pillars.
And you shall serve the Lord your God, and I will bless your bread, and your wine, and your water; and I will turn sickness away from you.
None shall be unfruitful or barren in your land; I will fulfil the number of your days.
And I will send fear before you, and confound all the nations among whom you come; and I will make all your adversaries fugitives.
And I will send hornets before you, and they shall drive out the Amorites, and Hivites, and Canaanites, and Hittites from before you.
I will not drive them out in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the land multiply against you;
little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you increase and inherit the land.

And I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the great river Euphrates; and I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hands, and cast them out from before you.
You shall make no covenant with them, nor with their gods;
neither shall they dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me; for if you serve their gods, these shall be a stumbling block to you.”
And He said to Moses, “Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, and Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and they shall bow down to the Lord from afar.
Moses alone shall approach God. They shall not approach, and the people shall not come up with them.”
Moses came in and related to the people all God’s words and ordinances. All the people answered with one voice, “We will do and obey everything the Lord has spoken.”
Moses wrote down all the Lord’s words. Moses rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain and twelve stones for Israel’s twelve tribes.
And he sent the young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered whole burnt offerings, and sacrificed calves as a sacrifice of deliverance to God.
Moses took half the blood and poured it into bowls; the other half he poured against the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. They said, “We will do and obey everything the Lord has spoken.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it over the people, saying, “Behold, the blood of the covenant the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.”
Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s council of elders went up,
and they saw the place where the God of Israel stood. What was beneath His feet was like sapphire brickwork, like the appearance of the firmament of heaven in its clarity.
Not one of Israel’s chosen men was missing. They appeared in the place of God, and ate and drank.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Come up to Me into the mountain, and remain there; and I will give you the tablets of stone, the law and the commandments which I have written to give them as law.”
Moses rose with Joshua, who attended him, and they went up the mountain of God.
They said to the elders, “Remain here until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are with you. If anyone has a dispute, let them approach them.”
Moses and Joshua went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
God’s glory descended on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called Moses from within the cloud.
The appearance of the Lord’s glory was like a blazing fire on the mountain’s summit before the sons of Israel.
Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. He remained there on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the sons of Israel, and receive firstfruits for Me from everyone whose heart is willing. You shall receive My firstfruits.
This is the firstfruit offering you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, double scarlet, spun fine linen, and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, blue skins, and decay-resistant wood;
sardius stones and stones for engraving, for the shoulder-piece and full-length robe.
And you shall make Me a sanctuary, and I will appear among you.
And you shall make it for Me according to all that I show you upon the mountain, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all its vessels; this is how you shall make it.
You shall make an ark of testimony of decay-resistant wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
You shall overlay it with pure gold, outside and inside, and make twisted gold mouldings around it.
You shall fashion four gold rings for it and place them on its four sides, two rings on one side and two on the other.
You shall make carrying poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with gold.
You shall put the poles through the rings on the ark’s sides to carry the ark with them.
The carrying poles shall remain fixed in the ark’s rings.
And you shall put into the ark the testimonies which I shall give you.
You shall make a propitiatory cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
You shall make two cherubim of worked gold and place them at the two sides of the propitiatory cover.
One cherub shall be made at this side and one at the other side of the propitiatory cover. You shall make the two cherubim at its two sides.
The cherubim shall spread their wings above, overshadowing the propitiatory cover with their wings. Their faces shall be toward one another, facing the propitiatory cover.
You shall place the propitiatory cover on top of the ark, and put into the ark the testimonies I will give you.

And I will be made known to you from there, and speak to you from above the propitiatory cover, from between the two cherubim upon the ark of the testimony, concerning all that I command you for the sons of Israel.
You shall make a table of pure gold, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
You shall make twisted gold mouldings around it.
You shall make a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and a twisted moulding around the rim.
You shall make four gold rings and put them at the four parts of its legs
beneath the rim; and the rings shall be holders for the carrying poles, that the table may be borne with them.
You shall make the carrying poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with pure gold, and the table shall be carried with them.
You shall make its dishes, incense cups, libation vessels, and cups for pouring libations. You shall make them of pure gold.
You shall place the bread of the Presence on the table before Me continually.
You shall make a lampstand of pure gold, of worked metal. Its stem, branches, bowls, knobs, and lilies shall be made from it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides, three from one side of the lampstand and three from the other.
There shall be three bowls shaped like little nuts, with a knob and lily on one branch. So it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand there shall be four bowls shaped like little nuts; on one branch shall be its knobs and lilies.
There shall be a knob under the two branches extending from it, and a knob under the four branches extending from it; so it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches shall be made from it, the whole worked from one piece of pure gold.
You shall make its seven lamps and set them on it, and they shall shine from one face.
You shall make its snuffer and supports of pure gold.
All these utensils shall be a talent of pure gold.
See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”
“You shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of spun fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn. You shall make them with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains shall have the same measure.
Five curtains shall be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another.
You shall make blue loops along the edge of one curtain at the joining side, and do the same along the edge of the outer curtain at the second joining.
You shall make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty along the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains one to another with the clasps; and the tabernacle shall be one.
You shall make hair curtains as a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
Each curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. The eleven curtains shall have the same measure.
You shall join five hair curtains by themselves and six by themselves, and double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tabernacle.
You shall make fifty loops along the edge of the middle hair curtain at the joining, and fifty along the edge of the curtain joining the second set.
You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and fasten the clasps into the loops, and join the hair curtains; and they shall be one.

You shall tuck under the surplus in the tabernacle’s hair curtains. You shall cover over the remaining half curtain; you shall cover over the surplus of the tabernacle’s hair curtains behind the tabernacle.
A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, from the excess length of the tabernacle’s hair curtains, shall cover the tabernacle’s sides on either side.
You shall make a covering for the tabernacle of rams’ skins dyed red, with coverings of blue skins above it.
You shall make posts of decay-resistant wood for the tabernacle.
You shall make each post ten cubits long, and the breadth of each post shall be a cubit and a half.
Each post shall have two tenons fitted opposite each other. You shall make all the tabernacle’s posts this way.
You shall make twenty posts for the tabernacle’s north side.
You shall make forty silver bases for the twenty posts, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the second side, to the south, there shall be twenty posts,
with their forty silver bases, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the sea, you shall make six posts.
You shall make two posts for the corners at the rear of the tabernacle.
They shall be equal below, and likewise equal at their tops, at one joining. You shall make both this way for the two corners.
There shall be eight posts with sixteen silver bases, two for each post at its two parts, and two for each post.
You shall make bars of decay-resistant wood, five for the post on one side of the tabernacle,
five for the post on the second side, and five for the rear post on the side toward the sea.
The middle bar shall pass through the middle of the posts from one side to the other.
You shall overlay the posts with gold and make gold rings into which you shall insert the bars. You shall overlay the bars with gold.
You shall erect the tabernacle according to the plan shown to you on the mountain.
You shall make a veil of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
You shall place it on four posts of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold, with gold capitals and four silver bases.
And you shall set the veil upon the posts, and bring in there, within the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.
You shall screen the ark of the testimony with the veil in the Holy of Holies.
You shall place the table outside the veil and the lampstand opposite it on the tabernacle’s south side; the table shall be on the north side.
You shall make a screen of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, the work of an embroiderer.
You shall make five posts for the curtain and overlay them with gold, with gold capitals, and cast five bronze bases for them.”
“You shall make an altar of decay-resistant wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square and three cubits high.
You shall make horns on its four corners, of one piece with it, and cover them with bronze.
You shall make a rim for the altar, its cover, bowls, meat forks, and firepan. You shall make all its utensils of bronze.
You shall make a bronze grating of network for it, with four bronze rings on its four sides.
You shall place them beneath the altar’s grating, and the grating shall reach halfway up the altar.
You shall make carrying poles of decay-resistant wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.
You shall put the carrying poles through the rings, and they shall lie along the altar’s sides when it is carried.
You shall make it hollow, of boards; as it was shown to you upon the mountain, so you shall make it.
You shall make a court for the tabernacle. On the side toward the southwest there shall be court hangings of spun fine linen a hundred cubits long on that side,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver rings and braces.
Likewise, on the side toward the east there shall be hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the rings, the posts’ braces, and their bases shall be silver-plated.
On the side toward the sea, across the court’s width, there shall be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
Across the court’s width on the south side there shall be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
The hangings on one side shall be fifteen cubits high, with three posts and three bases.
On the second side the hangings shall be fifteen cubits high, with three posts and three bases.
For the court’s gate there shall be a covering twenty cubits high, of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, embroidered needlework, with four posts and four bases.
All the posts around the court shall be silver-plated, with silver capitals and bronze bases.
The court’s length shall be a hundred by a hundred, its width fifty by fifty, and its height five cubits, with spun fine linen and bronze bases.
All the equipment, all the tools, and the court’s pegs shall be bronze.
You shall command the sons of Israel to bring you pure beaten olive oil, free of sediment, for the light, so that a lamp may burn continually

in the Tent of Testimony, outside the veil over the covenant. Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening to morning before the Lord, a perpetual statute throughout your generations on behalf of the sons of Israel.”
“And bring to yourself Aaron your brother and his sons from among the sons of Israel, to serve Me as priests: Aaron, and Nadab, and Abihu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
You shall make a holy robe for Aaron your brother, for honour and glory.
Speak to everyone skilled in understanding whom I have filled with a spirit of perception. They shall make Aaron’s holy robe for the sanctuary, in which he shall serve Me as priest.

These are the robes they shall make: a breastpiece, a shoulder-piece, a full-length robe, a tasselled tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy robes for Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
They shall take gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
They shall make the shoulder-piece of spun fine linen, the work of a skilled weaving embroiderer.
It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined to one another, fitted at the two sides.
The woven work of the shoulder-pieces upon it shall be made as one piece with it, of the same workmanship: gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.
You shall take two emerald stones and engrave the names of the sons of Israel on them,
six names on one stone and the six remaining names on the other, according to their generations.
With a stoneworker’s craftsmanship, like a seal engraving, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel.

You shall place the two stones on the shoulders of the shoulder-piece. They are memorial stones for the sons of Israel, and Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on his two shoulders before the Lord as a memorial concerning them.
You shall make small rosettes of pure gold,
you shall make two braided ornaments of pure gold, intertwined with flowers, and place the braided work on the rosettes along their shoulder-pieces in front.
You shall make an oracle-piece of judgments, embroidered work, according to the pattern of the shoulder-piece, of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.
It shall be square and doubled, a span long and a span wide.
You shall weave into it a fabric set with four rows of stones. The first row shall be a sardius, topaz, and emerald;
the second row a carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper;
the third row a ligure, agate, and amethyst;
the fourth row a chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. They shall be enclosed in gold and bound in gold according to their rows.
The stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
You shall make braided chains of pure gold for the oracle-piece.
And Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel upon the oracle-piece of judgment, upon his breast, when he enters into the sanctuary, as a memorial before God.

And you shall set the braided ornaments upon the oracle-piece of judgment; you shall set the chains upon both sides of the oracle-piece, and the two rosettes upon both shoulders of the shoulder-piece in front.

And you shall set Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece of judgment; and it shall be upon Aaron’s breast when he enters into the sanctuary before the Lord. And Aaron shall bear the judgments of the sons of Israel upon his breast before the Lord continually.
You shall make a full-length under-robe entirely blue.
And its neck opening shall be in the midst of it, with a border around the opening, the work of a weaver, its joining woven as one with it, so that it is not torn.

Around the under-robe’s lower hem you shall make little pomegranates like those of a flowering pomegranate tree, of blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen; likewise gold pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
Beside a gold pomegranate there shall be a bell and a floral ornament around the under-robe’s hem.
And Aaron’s sound shall be heard when he ministers, as he enters into the sanctuary before the Lord and as he goes out, so that he does not die.
You shall make a plate of pure gold and stamp on it like a seal: ‘The Lord’s consecrated thing.’
You shall fasten it to spun blue material so that it may rest on the headband, at the front of the headband.

It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall remove the sins of the holy things the sons of Israel consecrate, of every holy gift. It shall be on Aaron’s forehead continually, acceptable for them before the Lord.
The tunics’ tassels shall be of fine linen. You shall make a fine-linen turban and an embroidered sash.
You shall make tunics, sashes, and turbans for Aaron’s sons, for honour and glory.
You shall clothe Aaron your brother and his sons with these garments, anoint them, fill their hands, and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
You shall make linen undergarments for them to cover the nakedness of their flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs.

And Aaron and his sons shall wear them when they enter into the Tent of Testimony, or draw near to minister at the altar of the sanctuary; and they shall not bring sin upon themselves, lest they die. It shall be an everlasting statute for him and for his seed after him.”
“This is what you shall do for them: consecrate them to serve Me as priests. Take one calf from the herd and two rams without blemish,
unleavened loaves mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil. Make them from fine wheat flour.
Put them on one basket and present them on the basket, together with the calf and the two rams.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the Tent of Testimony and wash them with water.
Take the robes and clothe Aaron your brother with the full-length tunic, the shoulder-piece, and the oracle-piece. Fasten the oracle-piece to the shoulder-piece for him.
Put the headband on his head and the holy plate on the headband.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
Bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.
Gird them with sashes and put turbans on them. The priesthood shall be theirs for Me for ever. You shall consecrate Aaron’s hands and the hands of his sons.
Bring the calf to the doors of the Tent of Testimony. Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the calf’s head before the Lord, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
Slaughter the calf before the Lord at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
Take some of the calf’s blood and put it on the altar’s horns with your finger. Pour all the remaining blood at the altar’s base.
Take all the fat on the belly, the liver’s lobe, the two kidneys, and the fat on them, and place them on the altar.
Burn the calf’s flesh, skin, and dung with fire outside the camp, for it is a sin offering.
Take one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
Slaughter it, take the blood, and pour it against the altar on every side.
Divide the ram limb by limb, wash the entrails and feet with water, and place them on the pieces with the head.
Offer the whole ram on the altar as a whole burnt offering to the Lord, a fragrant aroma; it is a sacrifice to the Lord.
Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

And you shall slaughter it, and take of its blood, and put it upon the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, and upon the extremity of his right hand and of his right foot, and upon the lobes of his sons’ right ears, and upon the extremities of their right hands and of their right feet.

Take some blood from the altar and some anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his robe, and on his sons and their robes. He and his robe, and his sons and their robes, shall be holy. Pour the ram’s blood against the altar on every side.
Take the ram’s fat, the fat covering its belly, the liver’s lobe, the two kidneys and their fat, and the right foreleg, for this is a consecration;
also take one loaf made with oil and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread set before the Lord.
Put all these on the hands of Aaron and his sons and set them apart as a dedicated portion before the Lord.
Receive them from their hands and offer them on the altar of whole burnt offering as a fragrant aroma before the Lord, an offering to the Lord.
Take the breast from Aaron’s ram of consecration and set it apart as a dedicated portion before the Lord. It shall be your portion.
Consecrate the breast set apart and the foreleg of the contribution, which were set apart and taken from the ram of consecration for Aaron and his sons.

And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons by an everlasting statute from the sons of Israel; for it is a contribution, and shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel, from their sacrifices of deliverance, a contribution to the Lord.
Aaron’s holy robe shall belong to his sons after him, to be anointed in the garments and have their hands consecrated.
The priest who succeeds him from among his sons shall wear them for seven days; he shall enter the Tent of Testimony to minister in the holy places.
Take the ram of consecration and boil its flesh in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the ram’s flesh and the bread in the basket at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
They shall eat the things by which they were sanctified, to consecrate their hands and sanctify them. An outsider shall not eat them, because they are holy.
And if any of the flesh of the consecration sacrifice, or of the bread, remains until morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is a holy thing.
Do this for Aaron and his sons according to everything I commanded you. Consecrate their hands for seven days.
And you shall offer the calf for sin on the day of purification, and purify the altar when you perform consecration upon it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy; everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified.
This is what you shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs without blemish each day continually, a continual offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the second in the evening.
With one lamb offer a tenth measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of beaten oil, and a quarter hin of wine as a libation.
Offer the second lamb in the evening, with the same sacrifice and libation as in the morning, as a fragrant aroma, an offering to the Lord,
as a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord, where I will be made known to you, to speak to you.
There I will appoint Myself for the sons of Israel, and I will be sanctified in My glory.
I will consecrate the Tent of Testimony and the altar. I will also consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
I will be called upon among the sons of Israel and be their God.
They shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt to be called upon among them and to be their God.”
You shall make an incense altar of decay-resistant wood.
It shall be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high, with horns of one piece with it.
You shall overlay its grating, all its walls, and its horns with pure gold, and make a twisted gold rim around it.
You shall make two rings of pure gold beneath its twisted rim, on its two flanks, on the two sides, as holders for the poles used to carry it.
You shall make the poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with gold.
You shall put it opposite the veil over the ark of the testimonies, where I will make Myself known to you.
Aaron shall burn finely ground compounded incense upon it morning by morning, when he tends the lamps.
When Aaron lights the lamps in the evening, he shall burn incense upon it, a continual incense before the Lord throughout their generations.
You shall not offer other incense, an offering, or a sacrifice on it; you shall not pour a libation on it.

Once a year Aaron shall make expiation for it on its horns. With the blood of purification for sins, for expiation, once a year he shall purify it throughout their generations. It is most holy to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“When you number the sons of Israel in their visitation, each shall give the Lord a ransom for his soul, and no downfall shall come among them in their visitation.

This is what all who pass into the numbering shall give: half a didrachma, according to the holy didrachma. Twenty obols make the didrachma, and half a didrachma shall be the contribution to the Lord.
Everyone counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the contribution to the Lord.
The rich shall give no more and the poor no less than half a didrachma when giving the contribution to the Lord to make propitiation for your lives.

Receive the contribution silver from the sons of Israel and assign it to the work of the Tent of Testimony. It shall be a memorial for the sons of Israel before the Lord, to make propitiation for your lives.”
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Make a bronze basin with a bronze base for washing. Put it between the Tent of Testimony and the altar, and pour water into it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet with water from it.
When they enter the Tent of Testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die. When they approach the altar to minister and offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord,

they shall wash their hands and feet with water. When they enter the Tent of Testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die. This shall be a perpetual statute for him and his generations after him.”
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take spices: five hundred shekels of the choicest myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty, and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane,
five hundred sanctuary shekels of iris, and a hin of olive oil.
Make these into holy anointing oil, a compound prepared by a perfumer’s skill. It shall be holy anointing oil.
With it anoint the Tent of Testimony and the ark of the testimony,
the lampstand and all its utensils, and the incense altar,
the altar of whole burnt offerings and all its utensils, the table and all its utensils, and the basin and its base.
Consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Everyone who touches them shall be sanctified.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
Tell the sons of Israel: ‘This shall be holy anointing oil for you throughout your generations.
It shall not be applied to human flesh, and you shall not make anything like it for yourselves according to this composition. It is holy and shall be a holy thing to you.
Whoever makes anything like it, or gives any of it to an outsider, shall be destroyed from among his people.’”
The Lord said to Moses, “Take to yourself spices: stacte, onycha, fragrant galbanum, and clear frankincense, in equal portions.
They shall make them into incense, a perfumer’s compound, blended, a pure and holy work.
Grind some of it fine and place it before the testimonies in the Tent of Testimony, where I will make Myself known to you. It shall be most holy to you.
You shall not make incense for yourselves according to this composition. It shall be a holy thing to you for the Lord.
Whoever makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall perish from among his people.”
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Behold, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with a divine Spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of work,
to plan and design, to work in gold, silver, bronze, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen,
to work in stone and the woodworking crafts, and to perform every kind of work.
I have appointed him and Eliab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. I have given understanding to everyone discerning in heart, and they shall make everything I commanded you:
the Tent of Testimony, the ark of the covenant, the propitiatory cover upon it, and the tent’s furnishings,
the altars, the table and all its utensils, and the pure lampstand and all its utensils,
the basin and its base,
Aaron’s ministering robes and his sons’ robes for priestly service to Me,
the anointing oil and the compounded incense for the sanctuary. They shall make them according to everything I commanded you.”
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the sons of Israel, saying, ‘See that you keep My Sabbaths, for they are a sign with Me and among you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
You shall keep the Sabbaths, for this is holy to the Lord for you. Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death. Whoever does work on it, that soul shall be destroyed from among his people.
For six days you shall do your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord. Whoever does work on the seventh day shall surely be put to death.
The sons of Israel shall keep the Sabbaths, observing them throughout their generations: an everlasting covenant.
It is an everlasting sign between Me and the sons of Israel, for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and rested.’”
When He finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written with the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses delayed coming down from the mountain, they gathered against Aaron and said, “Arise, and make us gods to go before us. As for this Moses, the man who led us out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.”
Aaron said to them, “Take off the gold earrings from the ears of your wives and daughters, and bring them to me.”
All the people took off the gold earrings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He received them from their hands, fashioned them with an engraving tool, and made them into a cast calf. He said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”
When Aaron saw it, he built an altar opposite it and proclaimed, “Tomorrow is a feast of the Lord.”
He rose early the next day, offered whole burnt offerings, and brought a sacrifice of deliverance. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Go quickly from here and come down, for your people, whom you led out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly.

They have quickly transgressed the way you commanded them. They have made themselves a calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.’
Now leave Me alone, and in the heat of My wrath against them I will destroy them. I will make you into a great nation.”
Moses entreated the Lord God and said, “Why, O Lord, art Thou angry with Thy people, whom Thou didst lead out of the land of Egypt with great strength and Thine uplifted arm?
Let not the Egyptians say, ‘He led them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the earth.’ Cease from Thy fierce anger and be merciful concerning Thy people’s evil,

remembering Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Thy servants, to whom Thou didst swear by Thyself and speak, saying, ‘I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude’; and all this land which Thou didst say Thou wouldest give to their seed, they shall possess for ever.”
The Lord was appeased concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon His people.
Moses turned and came down the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hands, stone tablets written on both sides, on the one side and the other.
The tablets were God’s work, and the writing was God’s writing, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the people shouting, he said to Moses, “There is a sound of war in the camp!”
He said, “It is not the sound of those leading a song of victory or of defeat; it is the sound of those leading a wine-song that I hear.”
As he approached the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. In his anger Moses threw the two tablets from his hands and shattered them at the mountain’s foot.
He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it fine, scattered it on the water, and made the sons of Israel drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, “What did this people do to you, that you brought so great a sin upon them?”
Aaron said to Moses, “Do not be angry, my lord. You know this people’s impulse.
They said to me, ‘Make us gods to go before us. As for this Moses, the man who led us out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’
So I told them, ‘Whoever has gold ornaments, take them off.’ They gave them to me, I threw them into the fire, and this calf came out.”
Moses saw that the people were scattered, for Aaron had scattered them, to the delight of their enemies.
Moses stood at the camp’s gate and said, “Whoever is for the Lord, come to me!” All the sons of Levi gathered to him.

He said to them, “Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: ‘Each of you put his sword at his thigh. Go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and kill, each his brother, each his neighbour, and each the one nearest to him.’”
The sons of Levi did as Moses told them. As many as three thousand men of the people fell that day.
Moses said to them, “You have filled your hands today to the Lord, each at the cost of his son or brother, that a blessing may be given to you.”
After the next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to God, that I may make propitiation for your sin.”
Moses returned to the Lord and said, “I beseech Thee, O Lord: this people has committed a great sin and made themselves gods of gold.
Now, if Thou wilt forgive their sin, forgive it; but if not, blot me out of Thy book which Thou hast written.”
The Lord said to Moses, “If anyone has sinned before Me, I will blot him out of My book.
Now go down and lead this people to the place I told you. Behold, My angel goes before your face. On the day I visit, I will bring their sin upon them.”
The Lord struck the people because of the making of the calf Aaron made.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go up from here, you and your people whom you led out of the land of Egypt, to the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your seed.’
I will send My angel with you, before your face, and he shall drive out the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
I will bring you into a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up with you, lest I consume you on the way, for you are a stiff-necked people.”
When the people heard this grievous word, they mourned in mourning clothes.

The Lord said to the sons of Israel, “You are a stiff-necked people. Beware lest I bring another blow upon you and consume you. Now remove your splendid robes and ornaments, and I will show you what I will do to you.”
The sons of Israel removed their ornaments and splendid clothing from Mount Horeb onward.
Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and it was called the Tent of Testimony. Everyone seeking the Lord would go out to the tent outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went to the tent outside the camp, all the people stood watching, each at his own tent’s doors. They watched Moses go until he entered the tent.
When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud descended and stood at the tent’s door, and He spoke with Moses.
All the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the tent’s entrance. They rose and bowed down, each at his own tent’s entrance.
The Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses returned to the camp, but his young attendant Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent.
Moses said to the Lord, “Behold, Thou sayest to me, ‘Bring up this people,’ but Thou hast not shown me whom Thou wilt send with me. Thou hast said, ‘I know you above all, and you have grace with Me.’
If then I have found grace before Thee, reveal Thyself to me, that I may see Thee with understanding and find grace before Thee, and know that this great nation is Thy people.”
He said, “I Myself will go before you, and I will give you rest.”
Moses said to Him, “If Thou Thyself dost not go, do not bring me up from here.
How shall it truly be known that I and Thy people have found grace with Thee, unless Thou goest with us? Then I and Thy people shall be glorified above all the nations upon the earth.”
The Lord said to Moses, “I will also do this thing which you have asked, for you have found grace before Me, and I know you above all.”
Moses said, “Show me Thy glory.”
He said, “I will pass before you in My glory and proclaim My name, Lord, before you. I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and compassion on whom I will have compassion.”
He said, “You cannot see My face, for no man shall see My face and live.”
The Lord said, “Behold, there is a place beside Me; you shall stand upon the rock.
When My glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed.
Then I will remove My hand, and you shall see what is behind Me, but My face shall not appear to you.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to Me on the mountain. I will write upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets, which you shattered.
Be ready in the morning, come up to Mount Sinai, and stand before Me there on the mountain’s summit.
Let no one come up with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain. Neither sheep nor cattle shall graze near that mountain.”
Moses cut two stone tablets like the first. He rose early and went up Mount Sinai as the Lord commanded him, taking the two stone tablets.
The Lord descended in a cloud, stood beside him there, and called upon the name of the Lord.
The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, slow to anger, abundant in mercy and true,

preserving righteousness and showing mercy to thousands, taking away lawlessness, injustice, and sins, yet not cleansing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ lawlessness upon children and children’s children to the third and fourth generation.”
Moses quickly bowed to the ground and worshipped.
He said, “If I have found grace before Thee, let my Lord go with us, for this is a stiff-necked people. Thou shalt take away our sins and our lawlessness, and we shall be Thine.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Behold, I establish a covenant with you. Before all your people I will do glorious things never done in all the earth or among any nation. All the people among whom you are shall see the works of the Lord, for what I will do to you is marvellous.
Observe all that I command you. Behold, I am driving out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.
Take care, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, lest it become a stumbling block to you among you.
Tear down their altars, break their pillars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn their gods’ carved images with fire.
You shall not bow down to another god, for the Lord God, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
Make no covenant with the foreign inhabitants of the land, lest they prostitute themselves to their gods, sacrifice to their gods, invite you, and you eat of their sacrifices,
and take their daughters for your sons and give your daughters to their sons, and your daughters prostitute themselves to their gods and lead your sons to prostitute themselves to their gods.
You shall not make cast gods for yourself.

Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of new grain, for in the month of new grain you came out of Egypt.
Every male that opens the womb is Mine, every firstborn calf and firstborn sheep.

You shall redeem a firstborn beast of burden with a sheep; if you do not redeem it, you shall give its value. You shall redeem every firstborn of your sons. You shall not appear before Me empty-handed.
For six days you shall work, but on the seventh you shall rest; at sowing time and harvest you shall rest.
Keep the Feast of Weeks for Me, at the beginning of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the middle of the year.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the God of Israel.
When I drive nations out before your face and enlarge your borders, no one shall desire your land when you go up to appear before the Lord your God three times in the year.
You shall not offer the blood of My offerings with leaven, nor shall the sacrifices of the Passover feast remain until morning.
Bring the first produce of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You shall not offer a lamb in its mother’s milk.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Write these words for yourself, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and Israel.”
Moses was there before the Lord forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water. He wrote these words on the covenant tablets, the Ten Words.
As Moses came down from the mountain with the two tablets in his hands, he did not know that the appearance of the skin of his face had been glorified through speaking with Him.
Aaron and all Israel’s elders saw that the appearance of the skin of Moses’ face had been glorified, and they were afraid to approach him.
Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the assembly’s leaders returned to him. Moses spoke with them.
Afterward all the sons of Israel approached him, and he commanded them everything the Lord had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses entered before the Lord to speak with Him, he removed the veil until he came out. Then he told all the sons of Israel what the Lord had commanded him.
The sons of Israel saw that Moses’ face had been glorified. Moses replaced the veil over his face until he entered to converse with Him.
Moses assembled the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and said to them, “These are the things the Lord has said should be done.
For six days you shall do work, but on the seventh day there shall be rest, a holy Sabbath, a rest to the Lord. Everyone who does work on it shall die.
You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day. I am the Lord.”
Moses said to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, “This is what the Lord has appointed, saying,
‘Take from among yourselves an offering to the Lord. Everyone who welcomes it in his heart shall bring the Lord’s firstfruits: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, double-spun scarlet, spun fine linen, and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, skins dyed blue, and decay-resistant wood;
sardius stones and stones for engraving for the shoulder-piece and the full-length robe.
Let everyone wise in heart among you come and make everything the Lord has appointed:
the tent, its side curtains, its coverings and its stretching cords, its bars and its pillars;
the ark of the testimony and its carrying poles, the propitiatory cover, and the veil;
the hangings of the court and its pillars, the emerald stones, the incense, and the anointing oil;
the table and all its utensils;
the lampstand for the light and all its utensils;
the altar and all its utensils;
the holy robes of Aaron the priest and the robes in which they shall minister; the priestly tunics for Aaron’s sons, the anointing oil, and the compounded incense.’”
Then the whole congregation of the sons of Israel departed from Moses’ presence.
Everyone whose heart prompted him and whose soul was willing brought an offering to the Lord for all the work of the Tent of Testimony, for all its service, and for all the holy robes.
The men brought from the women, everyone whose heart approved: seals, earrings, rings, chains, bracelets, and every gold object—all who brought gold offerings to the Lord.
Everyone who had fine linen, skins dyed blue, or rams’ skins dyed red brought them.
Everyone contributing silver or bronze brought offerings to the Lord, and those who had decay-resistant wood for all the work of preparation brought it.
Every woman wise in heart spun with her hands and brought spun blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts stirred them with skill spun the goats’ hair.
The leaders brought the emerald stones and the stones for setting in the shoulder-piece and the oracle-piece,
and the compounds, the anointing oil, and the compounded incense.
Every man and woman whose mind inclined them to come and do all the work the Lord had commanded through Moses—the sons of Israel brought an offering to the Lord.
Moses said to the sons of Israel, “Behold, God has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the divine Spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge of all things,
to design in every craft, working gold, silver, and bronze,
to work stone and shape wood, and to carry out every work of skill.
He has put it in his mind to teach—both him and Eliab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with wisdom and understanding of mind to comprehend and do all the work of the sanctuary: weaving and embroidering in scarlet and fine linen, carrying out every work of design and embroidery.”

Bezalel, Eliab, and every person wise in understanding, who had been given wisdom and knowledge to understand how to do all the work for the holy service, worked according to all that the Lord had commanded.
Moses called Bezalel, Eliab, and all who possessed wisdom, to whom God had given knowledge in their hearts, and all who willingly came forward to the work to complete it.

They received from Moses all the contributions the sons of Israel had brought for all the work of the sanctuary, to carry it out. They continued receiving gifts from those who brought them, morning after morning.
All the skilled workers who were doing the work of the sanctuary came, each according to the work he was doing,
and they said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than is needed for the work the Lord commanded to be done.”
Moses gave a command and proclaimed in the camp, “Let neither man nor woman work any longer for the firstfruits of the sanctuary.” The people were restrained from bringing any more.
The work supplied was sufficient for the construction, with some left over.
Every skilled worker among the craftsmen made the holy robes for Aaron the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the shoulder-piece of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen.
The gold plates were cut into threads to be woven with the blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, a woven work.
They made joined shoulder sections for it on both sides,
a woven work intertwined together. They made it by itself from the same material, according to its workmanship: gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the two emerald stones, clasped and set in gold, engraved like seals with the names of the sons of Israel.
He put them on the shoulders of the shoulder-piece as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the oracle-piece with woven embroidery, like the workmanship of the shoulder-piece, of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen.
They made the oracle-piece square and doubled, a span long and a span wide when doubled.
A fabric set with four rows of stones was woven into it. The first row was a sardius, topaz, and emerald;
the second row a carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper;
the third row a ligure, agate, and amethyst;
the fourth row was a chrysolite, beryl, and onyx, enclosed in gold and bound in gold.
There were twelve stones bearing the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
They made braided chains of pure gold for the oracle-piece.
They made two gold rosettes and two gold rings, and put the two gold rings at the two ends of the oracle-piece.
They put the gold braids into the rings on both sides of the oracle-piece,
and the two braids into the two joinings. They put them on the two rosettes and on the shoulders of the shoulder-piece, facing forward.
They made two gold rings and put them at the two ends of the oracle-piece, on its edge toward the rear, on the inner side of the shoulder-piece.
They made two gold rings and put them on both shoulders of the shoulder-piece, below it at the front, by the joining above the shoulder-piece’s interwoven fabric.

He fastened the oracle-piece by its rings to the rings of the shoulder-piece with blue cord, interwoven into the shoulder-piece’s fabric so that the oracle-piece would not come loose from it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the robe beneath the shoulder-piece of woven work, entirely blue.
The opening of the robe was in its middle, woven and joined together, with a border around the opening so that it would not tear.
They made pomegranates at the lower hem of the robe, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, like a pomegranate tree in bloom.
They made gold bells and placed the bells at the hem of the robe, all around between the pomegranates,
a gold bell and a pomegranate at the hem of the robe all around, for ministry, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made woven tunics of fine linen for Aaron and his sons,
the turbans of fine linen, the headband of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of spun fine linen.
They made their sashes of fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet, the work of an embroiderer, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the gold plate, the holy consecration emblem, of pure gold. He wrote upon it letters engraved as on a seal: “A holy thing to the Lord.”
They put a blue band on it, to fasten it on the headband above, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made ten curtains for the tent.
Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long; all were alike. Each curtain was four cubits wide.
They made the veil of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, with woven cherubim.
They placed it on four pillars of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold. Their capitals were gold, and their four bases were silver.
They made the entrance veil of the Tent of Testimony of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen, with woven cherubim.
They made its five pillars and their rings, overlaid their capitals and their bands with gold, and made their five bases of bronze.
They made the court, with its southwest hangings of spun fine linen, a hundred by a hundred.
There were twenty pillars and twenty bases.
The north side was a hundred by a hundred, with twenty pillars and twenty bases.
On the side toward the sea were curtains of fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases.
On the east side were fifty cubits.
On the flank were hangings of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
On the second flank, on either side by the gate of the court, were curtains of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
All the curtains of the court were of spun fine linen.
Their pillars’ bases were bronze, their hooks silver, their capitals overlaid with silver, and all the court’s pillars overlaid with silver.
The veil for the court’s gate was embroidered in blue, purple, spun scarlet, and spun fine linen. It was twenty cubits long, with its height and breadth five cubits, matching the court’s hangings.
Its pillars were four, and its four bases were bronze; its hooks were silver, and its capitals were overlaid with silver;
and the pillars themselves were overlaid with silver. All the pegs around the court were bronze.
This is the arrangement of the Tent of Testimony, as appointed for Moses, with the service belonging to the Levites through Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, did as the Lord commanded Moses.
Eliab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, directed the woven, needleworked, and embroidered work, weaving in scarlet and fine linen.
Bezalel made the ark.
He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside.
He cast four gold rings for it, two on one side and two on the other.
The rings were wide enough for the carrying poles, so that the ark could be carried with them.
He made the propitiatory cover above the ark of gold.
He made the two gold cherubim,
one cherub at one end of the propitiatory cover and one cherub at its other end,
sheltering the propitiatory cover with their wings.
He made the table of presentation of pure gold.
He cast four rings for it, two on one side and two on the other, wide enough for the poles with which it would be carried.
He made the carrying poles of the ark and of the table, and overlaid them with gold.
He made the table’s utensils of gold: its dishes, incense vessels, ladles, and libation vessels with which to pour drink offerings.
He made the gold lampstand that gives light, with a solid shaft,
and its branches on both sides.
Shoots extended from its branches, three on this side and three on that side, corresponding to one another.

The lamp supports at their ends were nut-shaped and formed from them, as were the fittings on which the lamps would stand. The seventh fitting was at the end of the lamp support, at the top above; it was wholly solid gold.
He made seven gold lamps on it, its gold tongs, and its gold trays.
He overlaid the pillars with silver, cast gold rings for the pillar, and overlaid the bars with gold. He overlaid the pillars of the veil with gold and made gold hooks.
He also made the rings of the tent of gold, and the rings of the court and the rings for stretching the covering overhead of bronze.
He cast the silver capitals of the tent and the bronze capitals of the tent doorway and the gate of the court. He made silver hooks for the pillars; he silvered them.
He made the pegs of the tent and the pegs of the court of bronze.
He made the bronze altar from the bronze censers belonging to the men who had rebelled with the assembly of Korah.
He made all the altar’s utensils: its firepan, its base, its bowls, and its bronze meat forks.

He made a grating for the altar, a work of network beneath its firepan, below it as far as its middle. He put four bronze rings on the four sides of the altar’s grating, wide enough for the bars with which the altar would be carried.
He made the holy anointing oil and the compounded incense, the pure work of a perfumer.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze base from the mirrors of the women who fasted, who fasted at the doors of the Tent of Testimony on the day he set it up.

He made the basin so that Moses, Aaron, and his sons might wash their hands and feet from it. When they entered the Tent of Testimony, or approached the altar to minister, they washed from it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
All the gold worked into the objects, for all the work of the holy things, was the gold of the firstfruits: twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and twenty shekels, by the holy shekel.
The silver contribution from the enrolled men of the congregation was a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels,
one drachma per head, half a shekel by the holy shekel, for everyone passing into the enrolment from twenty years old upward: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the hundred capitals of the tent and the capitals of the veil: a hundred capitals for the hundred talents, a talent per capital.
They used the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels for the pillars’ hooks; he gilded their capitals and adorned them.
The bronze of the contribution was seventy talents and one thousand five hundred shekels.
From it he made the bases of the entrance of the Tent of Testimony,
the bases of the court all around, the bases of the court’s gate, the pegs of the tent, and the pegs of the surrounding court,
and the bronze grating of the altar, all the altar’s utensils, and all the equipment of the Tent of Testimony.
The sons of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses; so they did.
From the gold remaining from the contribution they made utensils for ministering before the Lord.
From the remaining blue, purple, and scarlet they made Aaron’s robes for ministry, to minister in the sanctuary.
They brought to Moses the robes, the tent and its utensils, its bases, its bars, and its pillars;
the ark of the covenant and its carrying poles;
the altar and all its utensils, the anointing oil, and the compounded incense;
the pure lampstand and its lamps, the lamps for burning, and the oil for the light;
the table of presentation and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
Aaron’s robes for the sanctuary and his sons’ robes for priestly service;
the hangings of the court and the pillars, the veil for the entrance of the tent and for the gate of the court, all the utensils of the tent, and all its equipment;
the leather coverings of rams’ skins dyed red, the coverings of blue skins, and the coverings for the remaining things;
the pegs, and all the equipment for the work of the Tent of Testimony.
The sons of Israel made all the equipment as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses saw all the work, and they had done it in the way the Lord commanded Moses; so they had done it. Moses blessed them.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“On the first day of the first month, at the new moon, you shall erect the Tent of Testimony.
You shall place the ark of the testimony and screen the ark with the veil.
Bring in the table and set out its presentation. Bring in the lampstand and put its lamps on it.
Place the gold altar for burning incense before the ark, and put a screening veil over the doorway of the Tent of Testimony.
Place the altar of offerings by the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
Set the tent about, and sanctify everything belonging to it all around.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the tent and everything in it. Sanctify it and all its utensils, and it shall be holy.
Anoint the altar of offerings and all its utensils. Sanctify the altar, and it shall be most holy.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the Tent of Testimony and wash them with water.
Clothe Aaron in the holy robes, anoint him, and sanctify him, and he shall serve Me as priest.
Bring his sons and clothe them in tunics.
Anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall serve Me as priests. They shall have an anointing for priesthood for ever, throughout their generations.”
Moses did everything the Lord had commanded him; so he did.
In the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt, at the new moon, the tent was erected.
Moses erected the tent, placed its capitals, inserted its bars, and erected its pillars.
He spread the curtains over the tent and placed the tent covering above it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He took the testimonies and put them into the ark, and placed the carrying poles beneath the ark.
He brought the ark into the tent, put up the screening veil, and screened the ark of the testimony, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the table in the Tent of Testimony, on its north side, outside the tent’s veil.
He set the bread of the Presence upon it before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the lampstand in the Tent of Testimony, on the south side of the tent.
He put its lamps in place before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the gold altar in the Tent of Testimony opposite the veil,
and burned the compounded incense on it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the altar of offerings by the doors of the tent.
He erected the court around the tent and the altar. Moses completed all the work.
The cloud covered the Tent of Testimony, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Moses could not enter the Tent of Testimony because the cloud overshadowed it and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Whenever the cloud rose from the tent, the sons of Israel set out with their belongings.
If the cloud did not rise, they did not set out until the day it rose.
For a cloud was over the tent by day, and fire was over it by night, in the sight of all Israel throughout all their journeys.
